proposals.title: Periodic points of the restricted stack-sorting maps s_{132,213} and s_{231,213}
proposals.exact_statement: Conjecture 5.1 of K. Berlow, 'Restricted Stacks as Functions' (arXiv:2008.01164v2, published Discrete Math. 344 (2021) 112571): 'The only periodic points of s_{132,213} and s_{231,213} are the identity and its reverse.' Here s_T (Def 1.3) sorts a permutation through a stack that must remain T-avoiding read top-to-bottom, each input element retried until it enters; periodic point: f^k(pi)=pi for some k>=1. Quantifiers: for every n and every pi in S_n, pi is periodic under the respective map iff pi in {id_n, id_n^r}.

primary_source.version: v2, 2021-06-11; published version exists (DOI 10.1016/j.disc.2021.112571) but was not retrieved

proposals.closest_predecessor: Theorems 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, Corollary 4.9 of the same paper fully classify periodic points of s_{123,132} (half-decreasing permutations, orbit size ceil((n+1)/2)) and s_{312,321} (half-increasing); Lemmas 4.3-4.4 give the normal-form method a proof would adapt.
proposals.closest_successor: arXiv:2405.01854 (2024, 'The Order of the (123,132)-Avoiding Stack Sort') restates a different Berlow conjecture and confirms activity; no resolution of Conjecture 5.1 found in this screen's search.
proposals.why_tractable: Decisive finite calculation exists and was executed: exact s_T simulation (validated against the source's proved cases on S_3..S_5: periodic sets matched half-decreasing/half-increasing classifications exactly, including counts 2/6/6) shows that on S_n for n=3..8 the periodic points of both s_{132,213} and s_{231,213} are exactly {id, reverse} (work/decisive-results.json, a_347483). A counterexample at any n is a one-permutation certificate.
proposals.decisive_next_calculation: Extend the exhaustive periodic-point search to n=9,10 with optimized code; in parallel pursue the structural route: show every permutation is drawn into the 2-cycle {id, reverse} by adapting the decreasing-half normal form (Lemma 4.3/4.4).
proposals.expected_certificate: Refutation: one permutation and its orbit (tiny; direct replay). Affirmation: full-scope proof, expected moderate size (pattern-avoidance stack algorithm as computable function + induction); no analysis.
proposals.formal_dependencies: Finite lists, decidable pattern containment, orbit counting; no axioms beyond standard.
proposals.open_risks: Published-version wording of Conjecture 5.1 not compared against arXiv v2; a full prior-art pass (Cerbai/Ferrari/Defant line, 2021-2026) is mandatory before investment; proof attempt may reduce to the source's own open problem with no shortcut.
proposals.not_a_discovery_note: Verifying the conjecture up to n=8 is not a discovery; only a refutation certificate or a complete proof counts.

proposals.title: Depth bound D(T) < 2 cfc(T) for every tree
proposals.exact_statement: Conjecture 3.6 of H. Chang, M. Ji, X. Li, J. Zhang, 'Conflict-free connection of trees' (arXiv:1712.10010v2): 'For a given tree T, D(T) < 2 cfc(T).' D(T) = minimum, over all priorities of choosing balanced edges in Algorithm 1, of the number of iterations until all components are singletons; cfc(T) = conflict-free connection number. Quantifiers: every tree T (every order).
proposals.closest_predecessor: Theorem 3.5 of the source (Algorithm 1 yields a CF coloring, so cfc(T) <= d(T) for every priority), Lemma 3.2 (d(T) >= max{Delta, ceil(log2 n)}), Theorem 2.5 (cfc(T) >= ceil(log2 n)), and the examples A_k with cfc(A_k)=k but k < D(A_k) < 2k showing D can exceed cfc.
proposals.closest_successor: None identified in this screen; a dedicated search for papers citing 'conflict-free connection' + algorithm depth is mandatory.
proposals.why_tractable: Pure finite-tree inequality. Exhaustive search executed here over all 94 unlabeled trees with n<=9 found zero trees with D(T) >= 2 cfc(T) (work/decisive-trees.json); in this range D < 2*Delta <= 2cfc always, so counterexamples can only live at larger n with small cfc - a bounded but nontrivial search regime (cfc <= D/2 <= (n-2)/2).
proposals.decisive_next_calculation: Push the exact D/cfc search to n<=14 using the cfc-critical decomposition and edge-ranking bounds from the same paper to prune; simultaneously attempt the proof route: from an optimal conflict-free connection coloring of T construct a balanced-edge removal priority of depth < 2 cfc(T) (the coloring's unique-color structure mirrors the balanced-edge splitting).
proposals.expected_certificate: Affirmation: full-scope constructive proof, moderate; formalization needs Algorithm 1 as a computable function on trees and an iteration-count bound. Refutation: one tree + its optimal priority/depth and cfc value (small but with a search-feasibility caveat).
proposals.formal_dependencies: Finite trees, edge colorings, path enumeration, algorithm iteration counts; no analysis.
proposals.open_risks: Exact cfc(T) computation grows fast; the conjecture is the source authors' own and may have a known counterexample or resolution not surfaced by this screen; D(T) definition depends on the paper's tie-breaking convention, which must be transcribed exactly from the body.

proposals.title: Equality of all generalized commuting probabilities forces equal central quotient orders
proposals.exact_statement: Conjecture 6.3 of Y. Cherniavsky, A. Goldstein, V. E. Levit, R. Shwartz, 'Hultman Numbers and Generalized Commuting Probability in Finite Groups' (arXiv:1403.3868v2; published J. Integer Seq. 20 (2017), A.3.2): if Pr^{2n}(G1) = Pr^{2n}(G2) for every n >= 0, then |G1/Z(G1)| = |G2/Z(G2)|. Pr^{2n}(G) = Pr(a_1...a_{2n} = a_{2n}...a_1) with a_i uniform in G.

primary_source.version: v2, 2014-10-02; published JIS version at cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL20/Levit/levit4.html (not retrieved; formula transcriptions in the arXiv HTML may be lossy)

proposals.closest_predecessor: Theorems 6.1/6.2 of the source (lim Pr^{2n} = 1/|G'|; isoclinic groups have equal Pr^{2n} for all n) and the source's own order-64 examples; the conjecture is the source's own open question.
proposals.closest_successor: 'Signed Hultman numbers...' (J. Algebra Appl. / doi 10.1007/s10801-021-01089-9, 2021) and arXiv:2605.02071 (2026, 'Higher Commutativity in Finite Groups: Exact Asymptotics and Finite Spectrum') are adjacent; neither screen as answering Conjecture 6.3.
proposals.why_tractable: All quantities are finite-group computations. Pilot scan executed here (11 hand-coded groups, orders 8-32, Pr^{2n} for n<=3 by exact enumeration, work/decisive-results.json b_327474): all pairs with equal sequences were isoclinic with equal |G/Z|, consistent with the conjecture and showing no cheap refutation in the easiest families. A refutation, if it exists, needs a full small-group scan and is certified by two explicit groups.
proposals.decisive_next_calculation: Enumerate all groups of order <= 64 (GAP SmallGroups; not installed in this environment - flagged as a dependency), compute (Pr^2, Pr^4, Pr^6) exactly per group, and compare sequences; for any equal-sequence pair with different |G/Z|, certify equality for all n via identical class-multiplication tables (sufficient by the source's Section 5 formulas, which must first be verified against the published JIS text).
proposals.expected_certificate: Refutation: two explicit groups (Cayley tables) + computed rational sequences + differing central quotient orders; verifiable by direct enumeration, moderate Lean size. Affirmation of the conjecture: likely hard/unbounded - if the scan finds nothing, park.
proposals.formal_dependencies: Explicit finite group tables, rational arithmetic, conjugacy-class computation; no external libraries in the certificate.
proposals.open_risks: No GAP in this environment (guard-capped lane); Pr^{2n} formula transcriptions from arXiv HTML are unreliable (a transcription of formula (25) fails the n=1 sanity check against Gustafson k(G)/|G|, so the published text must be authoritative); a counterexample may not exist at order <= 64; equality-for-all-n certification needs the class-table route to work.
